Transfer the automation to a new owner so that its executions are counted again
quiz.explain: Automate uses at-least-once semantics, so actions and functions must handle reruns gracefully; prompt wording and ownership do not prevent duplicate executions.

quiz.q: A team built a chatbot that proposes maintenance reschedules. Management eventually wants it to run without anyone watching. Which plan fits the documentation and the course's idea of progressive automation?
choices: Run it unattended from day one and add reviews only if users complain
Give the chatbot the automation owner's broad permissions so its edits never fail
Add a sentence to the instructions telling the model to be careful with reschedules
Have it propose changes through an Action tool that needs user confirmation, publish it as a Function and test it in AIP Evals, then automate with a documented owner, review step and recovery path
quiz.explain: Human confirmation first, evidence from Evals next, and automation with planned identity, review and recovery follows the docs; prompt wording and broad permissions are not controls.

days.recap: AIP Logic builds LLM functions from blocks over the Ontology, AIP Chatbots answer and act through retrieval context and tools, Automate runs effects on conditions as the owner, and AIP Evals measures quality across runs; keep humans in the loop with confirmed actions and widen automation only on evidence.

days.title: Final Review: Foundry Aware Across All Three Sections

concepts.heading: What the exam looks like
concepts.body: Foundry Aware is Palantir's free foundation-level exam, which completing the Foundry & AIP Aware course makes you eligible for. It has 60 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes, is open note and open website, and retakes are allowed. Palantir does not publish a pass mark or domain weights; this bank maps the course's three sections (Getting Acquainted with Foundry & AIP, Building Blocks for Developers, Applying Foundry & AIP in the Real World) to domains D1-D3 and weights them equally, which is the bank's own assumption. Two minutes per question leaves time to look things up, but open note rewards knowing where an answer lives, not searching from scratch for every question.

concepts.heading: Section 1: the platform and the Ontology
concepts.body: Foundry & AIP model decisions, not only data: data, logic, action and security meet in the Ontology, whose objects and links are the nouns and whose actions, powered by logic such as functions, are the verbs that people, apps and AI agents share under one security model. South of the Ontology (course framing) are data sources, logic sources and systems of action; north are analytics, Workshop workflows, Automate automations and products built with the Ontology SDK. Projects and group roles grant access, markings restrict it mandatorily and follow the data, evals build trust before automation widens, Global Branching tests changes end to end, and Apollo delivers the software. The first workflow runs sources into datasets, a Pipeline Builder pipeline, objects and links, and a Workshop app with actions.

concepts.heading: Section 2: building blocks for developers
concepts.body: In Data Connection, a source holds the location, credentials, worker and egress policy, while a sync chooses the data and the output dataset; network, certificate and permission errors are fixed at their own layer. REST APIs are ingested with code: a REST API source imported into a code repository, an external transform calling it, then a commit and a build, since a commit alone writes no dataset. For an app, back each object type with a dataset at the object's grain, pick a unique, stable primary key, choose link types by cardinality and change data through action types. Workshop apps are widgets wired by variables and events; forms come from actions, and module and data permissions decide what each user sees.

concepts.heading: Section 3: applying it in the real world
concepts.body: Scope a use case as a time-bound effort by a dedicated team for one recurring operational decision, start from the outcome, check what data already exists, and position Foundry & AIP as the layer that integrates existing systems and writes decisions back. Machinery models a process as states and transitions mined from a log of state changes and shows where objects get stuck. AIP Logic, AIP Chatbots, Automate and AIP Evals build agentic workflows: actions under known permissions, human confirmation for consequential changes, effects that run as the automation owner, and evals across several runs before automation widens.

concepts.heading: Patterns that answer many questions
concepts.body: Across all three sections the same choices recur. Prefer the simplest tool that meets the stated need: retrieval context before tools, a dashboard when nobody needs to act, a drawn model for a new process. Prefer controls over instructions: an action with confirmation rather than a prompt saying "be careful", markings rather than unmarking for convenience, a pinned function version rather than hoping nothing changes. Prefer evidence before change: Evals before automating, a branch before merging, the first bad stage before rebuilding. Distrust options that replace systems of record, grant broad access, copy all data "just in case" or reach for a bigger model or longer prompt.

examPoints: When two options both work, prefer the one that integrates existing systems, keeps permissions and markings intact and adds human review, over rip-and-replace, broad grants or unattended automation.

When a question names a need, match it to the product built for it: Data Connection to ingest, Pipeline Builder to transform, the Ontology to model, Workshop to act, Machinery for processes, AIP Logic and Chatbots for LLM work, Automate for triggers and AIP Evals for testing.

quiz.q: Which statement about the Foundry Aware exam matches the facts this guide gives?
choices: It has 95 questions in 3 hours with a 70% pass mark, like the Data Engineer Associate exam
It is a hands-on live exam in a real Foundry environment
It has 60 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes, is open note and open website, is free, allows retakes and has no published pass mark
It is closed book with 60 questions and a published 70% pass mark
quiz.explain: Foundry Aware is the free foundation exam: 60 multiple-choice questions, 120 minutes, open note and open website, retakes allowed, pass mark not published; the 95-question, 3-hour, 70% format belongs to the Data Engineer and AI Engineer Associate exams.

quiz.q: A sponsor wants an AI agent to approve supplier invoices automatically from day one, before any data is connected. Which plan best reflects what all three course sections teach?
choices: Connect the sources, model invoices and an approval action in the Ontology, let people use an app with AI suggestions, test the AI with AIP Evals, then automate step by step with a planned owner and recovery path
Start with the agent and a long prompt describing invoices, and connect data later if its answers look wrong
Replace the ERP's invoice module with Foundry first so that the agent has one system to work in
Grant the agent Owner on every project so that missing permissions never block an approval
quiz.explain: Data in, Ontology and actions, people in the loop, evidence from Evals and then progressive automation; skipping data, replacing the ERP or granting broad access are the distractors the course warns against.

days.recap: Foundry Aware covers the platform and Ontology, the developer building blocks and real-world use: start from a decision, bring data in, model it in the Ontology, let people act through apps, add AI under the same permissions, prove it with evals and automate step by step; the exam has 60 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes, open note, free, with retakes allowed.
